summary: A 1913 dwelling-and-light at Naufrage on PEI's northeast shore, replaced by a 1967 concrete tower; a widow kept the light after her keeper husband drowned.

structures.note: Octagonal concrete tower; LighthouseFriends gives 13.4 m and service from 27 September 1967; Lighthouse Directory dates it 1968
Two-storey combined dwelling and lighthouse; lantern removed; privately owned; sold 2013 as a rental

access.note: Sources disagree. LighthouseFriends describes a walkway from Harbour Road made by the Friends group and says the grounds and tower are closed. The Lighthouse Directory lists the site and tower as closed, private property. The 1913 building is private and can be seen from a public road.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner); Friends of Shipwreck Point (site manager)

events.note: Combined wooden dwelling and lighthouse erected by the Annandale Lumber Company, $3,213.81 (report and LighthouseFriends)
Fourth-order dioptric lens in the 1913 lantern
Keeper Francis MacKinnon drowned setting lobster traps on 12 May 1917; his widow Sarah kept the light
Cellar dug out beneath the 1913 dwelling
Light operated year round, 1942 to 1945, for wartime Commonwealth pilot training (Society's account)
Final keeper Hugh Boniface MacDonald retired; light automated
Octagonal concrete tower built a short distance west of the 1913 building by Schurman's Limited; in service 27 September 1967
Tower replaced the dwelling's light; the 1913 building was left vacant (Rowlett gives 1968)
The 1913 building sold in May 2013 to private owners
Local group that applied for ownership of the lighthouse in 2015 received a $28,540 grant for repairs; transfer still pending in September 2024 (Rowlett)

corrections.why: The record's 13.5 m standing tower is the 1967 concrete tower (LighthouseFriends; Coast Guard list height 13.5 m). The 1913 date belongs to the dwelling-and-lighthouse, which should be a separate structure record (role dwelling, privately owned).

corrections.proposed: Canadian Coast Guard / federal (for the 1967 tower; the 1913 building is privately owned)
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory both give the Canadian Coast Guard as owner of the active light.
LighthouseFriends gives 27 September 1967 as the date the new tower went into service. The Lighthouse Directory's 1968 is the disputed date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record and Wikidata disagree (active versus inactive). The Coast Guard list shows the 1967 tower active, and the Lighthouse Directory marks the 1913 building inactive since 1968. Both are true of different structures.
Coast Guard list 25.6 m for the current tower; the Lighthouse Directory gives 25.5 m; the Society gives 26.2 m for the 1913 light. Current figure is 25.6 m.
1913 is the dwelling-and-lighthouse; the active tower was built in 1967 (LighthouseFriends) or 1968 (Lighthouse Directory).

notes_for_editor: Access conflicts: LighthouseFriends describes a walkway built by the Friends group from Harbour Road and gives 'Grounds/tower closed'; the Lighthouse Directory says site and tower closed (private property); the Society says the old building is on private property and viewable from a public road. The record's 'access: closed' is kept. Tower date: 27 September 1967 (LighthouseFriends; the Society gives electrification in September 1967) against 1968 (Lighthouse Directory; Wikidata). Ownership: the record says private; LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory give the Coast Guard as owner of the active tower. The Society says the 1913 building was 'sold to the former keeper' when automated in 1966 and sold again in May 2013; the Lighthouse Directory says sold in 2013 and inactive since 1968. Keeper statement and works lists in the 1915 and 1919 reports are OCR tables: 'Shipwreck point F. McKinnon' (1915, p.62) and 'Digging out the cellar under lighthouse and dwelling' (1919, p.33) were checked on the page images (the keeper row sits on one printed line with 'Oct. 30, 1913'; the cellar line sits level with the Shipwreck point label in the Prince Edward Island section); the combined dwelling entry in the 1915 new-aids list (p.43) also sits level with the Shipwreck Point label, contractor 'The Annandale Lumber Co.'; the Annandale contract and $3,213.81 line also match LighthouseFriends, and the 1918 cellar date matches LighthouseFriends. The keeper's appointment date printed beside F. McKinnon in the same statement (30 October 1913) is read by position and not used in the story. The Department reports in the corpus do not list the 1917 drowning or the Sarah MacKinnon appointment (the corpus ends in 1924 and the statements from 1917 on were not found), so those rest on LighthouseFriends and the Society, both secondary. The oral history of a 1719 wreck is attributed to LighthouseFriends and no document is cited; left as an attributed claim. The Naufrage Chronicling America search returned no hits for Shipwreck Point, Prince Edward Island in 1913 to 1925. LighthouseFriends cites an Eastern Kings, P.E.I. website (Waldron H. Leard) and Carol Livingstone's 2002 binder on PEI lighthouses; neither was read. The 1913 keeper's dwelling is privately owned and rented; its owners are not named. Naufrage Lighthouse Cottage is not named. Tower height: the Coast Guard list and the Lighthouse Directory give 13.5 m; LighthouseFriends gives 13.4 m (the story states the disagreement). Neil: the Society says he showed his mother how to look after the light; LighthouseFriends says he instructed 'some gentlemen' (both stated in the story). The 'no documentary record' remark was removed from the story: LighthouseFriends gives the 1719 story as oral history only.
